findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.12: (A) Observed plastic at top of interior cavity of microwave in kitchen to be peeling. Replace microwave. The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.11: (D) Observed blade of counter mounted can opener in kitchen to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize can opener blade. FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: (A) Observed opened can of sausage gravy and 2 open bags of hard boiled eggs in cooler to not be date marked. Items were marked with date of 3/28/23 during inspection. Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: 3-501.13: Observed 2 bags of ground beef being thawed in sink with no running water. TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
Some of the food handlers have expired. Have all employees who participate in food handling or handling of clean utensils provide current food handler certificated.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreements were not available at the time of inspection. Employee health documents were provided. Employee health policy was discussed with emphasis on knowledge required by management and staff on reporting illness and time frame for exclusion from food handling depending on reportable symptoms versus being diagnosed with and/or potentially exposed to foodborne pathogens. Reporting agreements were signed by food service staff during the inspection. Ensure all staff that have the potential to work in the food service area are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for the food service staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure for disinfection after a vomit and/or diarrhea event was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach and peroxide disinfectant are both available for use. Facility manager was advised to ensure staff are educated on which chemical will be used and proper use of the chemical during cleanup and disinfection process.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee helping in breakfast area was observed washing hands without proper technique. Employee used their hands to shut off the manual faucet prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with emphasis on shutting off the faucet by using paper towels as a barrier or use of an elbow or forearm to avoid contamination of freshly washed hands. 
-Breakfast attendant used a wiping cloth to wipe hands. Wiping cloths and other cloth towels should not be used to wipe hands. If hands need to be wiped, then they should be properly washed and disposable paper towels should be used to wipe hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Breakfast attendant and employee helping with breakfast service were observed putting on gloves and going between glove changes without first washing their hands. Handwashing prior to putting on gloves and frequently between glove changes was discussed. More frequent handwashing was observed.
-Employee helping in the breakfast area was observed entering the kitchen and putting on gloves without first washing hands. That employee then left the kitchen and proceeded to another area prior to returning to help with food service. Glove use was discussed as it appeared the same gloves may have been worn between tasks. The employee stated hands were washed in the restroom between glove changes before returning to the breakfast area. Employee was not observed washing hands in the kitchen and was advised on handwashing upon entering the kitchen even if hands were just washed in the restroom and before putting on gloves or working with food. Employee was later observed washing hands between tasks and glove changes.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, upon entering the work area, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Breakfast attendant began handwashing process at the sprayer sink by the dish machine. Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink was discussed. Staff were observed washing hands at the designated handsink for the remainder of the inspection.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee helping in breakfast area used a gloved hand to shut the ringer off on their cell phone and continued stocking food items without changing gloves. Proper glove use was discussed.  
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of quat sanitizer in the kitchen was observed at 0ppm. Product was discarded and replaced with fresh solution from the dispenser in the laundry room. Fresh solution was observed at 400ppm. 
-Quat dispenser in the kitchen was not functioning properly. Dispensed chemical was at 0ppm. Call for service was made. Ensure all employees know to prepare quat solutions using the dispenser in the laundry room until the dispenser in the kitchen is repaired and able to dispense product at proper concentration (effective range 150-400ppm). 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-502.11 Temperature gauge on the dish machine was not functioning properly at the time of inspection. The gauge was not moving beyond 150F during a ware washing cycle. Call for service to get the temperature gauge repaired. 
Water temperature measuring devices shall be maintained in good repair and be accurate within the intended range of use.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11  (Pf) Food establishment does not have food cooling equipment with adequate capacity for current operations. Provide equipment for cooling food, and holding cold food, that is sufficient in number and capacity to cool food rapidly to required temperatures within the required timeframes. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 4-301.11. The Vitality Juice machine is not currently holding food at the proper temperature. A service call has been placed and the machine is going to be repaired or replaced. If the machine is not functioning by the follow up date, please contact me prior to the date.  Also, do not use machine until it is holding properly.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location on the floor in the dry storage area of the kitchen. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.  Observed  boxes of waffle mix on the floor of the dry storage area. Store food and all food related items properly protected.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination at holders in the food service. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11. Make sure to clean crumbs and dust out of the utensil holders daily and maintain free of accumulated curmbs.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the following non food contact surfaces: 1) fronts of cabinets especially at handles 2) front of  fan cover at cold holding in food service 3) inside of cbinet to the right of the ice holding area in food service. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
According to the manufacturer the juice machine should be holding juice at 41F or below. Water to the unit should be 37F or below. The air temperature of the machine is 49.8F.  The juices should be discarded and the machine serviced so that it runs according to manufacturer specifications. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
Juices were discarded except for one OJ which was just placed into the unit this morning. It was pulled and put back into the cooler.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Observed boxes of waffle mix to be stacked on the floor. Do not place food containers directly on the floor. 750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Upon arrival the dish machine had been in use for the day. The dish machine has 0ppm of chlorine. It is noted that the draw tube was lifted out of the protective straw that is provided. The tube was placed back into the sanitizer and the machine was primed. It is now functioning. Still suggest service to ensure the machine continues to function according to manufacturer specifications. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration. Eco Lab rep is on site.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed waffle batter in the cooler at 70F. It had just been made. There was no label on the container. Properly date mark and time the batter to ensure that it is cooling properly. Also make sure to use small enough portions (4 inches or less) to ensure that the batter cool properly (in the 4 hour time limit) Proper labels were added to the batter. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Milk lines are not cut at a 45 degree angel and holding milk in lines. Yogurt on ice is 48F in the top of the container. Place yogurt deeper into ice and make sure to cut lines on the milk dispenser so that they drain properly. MIlk lines were cut and Yogurts discarded. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) .

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: The dish machine has a gross accumulation of lime on the inside and on the drain basket. Clean and maintain clean. Test dish machine daily to ensure that proper sanitizing is taking place. 750-830 All dish washing machines shall be thoroughly cleaned at least once a day or more often when necessary to maintain them in satisfactory operating condition.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils to be stored in cardboard box in the dry storage area. Box was soiled. Box was removed, utensils were placed in the sink to be cleaned. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Sausages in hot holding unit had internal temperature of 120F-125F. Attendant was asked what the cooking temperature was prior to placing product in the warmer. Final cooking temperature was not checked. Attendant prepared a fresh batch of sausage, which was cooked to 161F prior to being placed in the hot holding unit for service.

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135F/above while on display and service.
**Make sure the cooking temperature is checked prior to placing foods in hot holding wells for service. The only way to know if foods have reached proper temperature is to check the internal temperature with a clean, calibrated stem thermometer**

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Dish machine sanitizing concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer line was primed, but the concentration remained at 0ppm after another full cycle. Maintenance Manager changed the chemical hose and as the line was getting primed the pump stopped working (motor got overheated). Breakfast Attendant setup the 3 part sink for manual ware washing. Wall mounted quat dispenser was used to setup sanitizer compartment (200ppm). 
EcoLab was scheduled to come out this week anyway, but a call for service was made during the inspection 
After hose was changed and the motor cooled down to allow for operation the dish machine sanitizer concentration was observed at 50-100ppm chlorine.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
**Check the sanitizer daily to verify proper sanitizing concentration at the dish machine (50-100ppm chlorine) and the wall mounted dispenser (150-400ppm quat)**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors along walls/in corners and under equipment were observed to be soiled in the dry storage room (under shelves, cooler, & freezer), and in the kitchen (under/behind ice machine, sprayer sink, and dish machine). Maintenance worker began cleaning in the dry storage area during the inspection.
Clean the floors throughout under equipment/along walls and in corners daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.150 - Scrambled eggs in pan of warm water had surface and internal temperatures at 97F-99F & 90F respectively. Attendant stated three bags of eggs were removed from the oven, and only two of the bags were used. Third bag was sitting out for ~15-20 minutes. Bag of eggs was reheated to 167F prior to placing in breakfast area hot holding well for service.

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above except during the cooling process. Store and maintain hot foods at 135F/above. If extra product is not immediately needed then hot hold foods in the oven until ready for service.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Sanitizer concentration at dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. Attendant noted the bottle looked new but was unsure as to when the new bottle was hooked up at the dish machine. The chemical line was primed. Sanitizer dispensed at proper concentration of 50ppm after a couple full cycles of the dish machine.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
Make sure chemical lines are primed when new bottles are hooked up to ensure chemicals are pulling through the lines. Use test strips to check the sanitizer concentration the first run of every day, after new sanitizer is hooked up, and periodically throughout the day.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1100 & 1060 - Leak was present at the underside of the dish machine. At time of inspection it was difficult to determine where the leak originated. Maintenance Manager stated he would check the machine/make repairs later today after breakfast attendant was done for the day.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor under shelves and cold holding units in dry storage room were soiled with food, single service articles, and general debris. Clean the floor as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors shall be maintained clean.  Attendant began cleaning the floor at time of inspection.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Packets of cream cheese and whipped butter had internal temperatures of 57F/61F and 58F/59F respectively. Bowls holding products were placed on ice, but ice had melted. Packaging for whipped butter and cream cheese state "keep refrigerated". All of the unused packets were to be discarded at the end of breakfast today (packets are typically placed back in cooler at the end of breakfast). Discussed options for cold holding and time control with Breakfast Area Attendant and Manager. Time Control Policy sheet was provided and filled out during inspection. Time for cream cheese and whipped butter packets will be tracked with a 30 day tracking sheet. The tracking sheet will be housed at the cooler on a clipboard. In the meantime, the Manager is going to look into obtaining more cold holding containers similar to the one currently used to hold hard boiled eggs at the breakfast counter (container with hard boiled eggs was holding product below 41F). Adhere to time control policy until a practice is established that will maintain the cream cheese and whipped butter packets at 41F/below.
Cold foods must be maintained at 41F/below unless time control is being used.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512 & 530 - Breakfast Attendant was observed chewing gum while working with food and equipment. When asked to dispose of gum it was spit into Attendants hand prior to being placed in trash can. Attendant then returned to working in dish area without washing hands. Attendant washed hands upon request of inspector. Proper handwashing, when to wash hands, and appropriate personal hygiene practices with food/beverages were discussed.
Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas, this includes gum and candy. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Wash hands before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and between tasks as needed.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b -The following food contact surfaces were soiled with crumbs, dust, and/or food splash: A) trays, domes, and tongs in dry storage used to serve cookies the previous day; B) wall fan in kitchen; & C) inside kitchen microwave. Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
**Trays, domes and tongs were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Upon returning serving trays, tongs, etc. to the kitchen area those items must be placed in a designated dirty dish area if they are not going to immediately be placed through ware washing process. Do not store soiled food equipment in areas where it may be mistaken for clean equipment and used.**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled with crumbs, dust, and general debris: A) bottom inside cooler; B) bottom inside freezer; C) counter under convection oven; D) cabinet below 3 part sink; & E) counters under microwaves.
Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
